questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: Actually, three of the options did: Both academic and career opportunities, but also the exploration of the English culture

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: My options were limited, but the bettering of my English speaking capabilities was a priority for me

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. The incoming exchanges team at Kent are really super

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Again, the incoming exchanges team are really quick to reply and give solid advice and help

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: We really only had one option for accommodation, as the other types of housing are for students who live on campus for longer than 1 semester

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Pretty decent cooking facilities in the accommodation, but there were also catering options - I just cooked my own food mostly

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Overall, it's pretty good. Better than what I've heard about other places

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was pretty intuitive. The module selection thing is a bit janky, but overall it's pretty good. The system seemed surprisingly up-to-date

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Again, I have to give kudos to the incoming exchanges team at Kent - they helped me with just about everything

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: They had some issues with certain courses not being formed, as they had a professor leave right before semester start, so that was a bit disappointing, but it is no fault of theirs really. Overall, I was relatively succesful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: When in doubt, as the incoming exchanges team

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The master of laws is a socio-legal education, which has very little relevance to jobs and practice. Also, there was quite a lot of confusion about simple formatting and not a clear, consistent line across the courses. Overall, I was really quite disappointed in the academic aspect. I would not recommend people go here for academic reasons.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was fine, but i would defer to my answer to the overall academic level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was relatively similar, but I would say that the teachers felt less qualified in certain aspects of the teaching. Still, they were really nice and relatively competent.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Commercial Credit, Policing, and International Cultural Heritage Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Commercial Credit. It was pretty elementary but the teaching featured a lot of discussion which was pretty nice.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not really any. The figures above do not accurately account for things such as social spending, as I would not include that as "other fees" given that they will vary heavily depending on the student in question.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Not really any. Prices in the UK are comparable to Denmark, although everything is generally a little cheaper in the UK.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great sport facilities, as exchanges automatically get full access to everything.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds of sports, clubs for just about everything, and they had societies for pretty much all nationalities where student not of said nationality could participate anyways. E.g., I went to several events with both the French and Spanish societies.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Get involved with the nationality-based societies, as they generally have the most stuff planned.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to London or any of the academic cities, e.g., Cambridge and Oxford, as the nightlife is great there. If you enjoy a beer, do partake in British pub culture, as that truly is a national treasure.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The UK is not dissimilar to Denmark in terms of culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just get out there - people are really nice! Do go to the speedfriending event in the first week - it's an easy opening, as some of the local students participate as well

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None really. It was just a bit annoying that people always say "how are you?" even when passing each other, but I was aware of that before I went there.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I thoroughly enjoyed pub culture

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1. Do not go for academic purposes. 2. Go to local pubs - even on weekdays for a couple at least. 3. Socialise with the locals and not just the other exchanges - this would also include the students doing a full master's

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The cultural aspects, though centered around drinking (much like Danish culture), and language proficiency.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I had some unfortunate encounters with some of the other exchange students

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
